docs.title: PIDL
docs.text:
Protocol Interaction Description Language - A JSON-based DSL for describing protocol choreography that compiles to diagrams.

PIDL models protocols as directed interaction graphs between entities, enabling generation of sequence diagrams, data flow diagrams, and other visualizations. It's designed for protocols where the primary concern is "who talks to whom, in what order" rather than message schemas or transport details.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• JSON-based DSL for describing protocol flows
  • Multiple output formats: PlantUML, Mermaid, Graphviz DOT, D2, SVG
  • Animated SVG with CSS flow visualizations and moving dots
  • Network boundary diagrams for trust zone visualization
  • SVG templates: default, minimal, sketch, blueprint, dark, high-contrast
  • Accessibility: WCAG AA compliant high-contrast template
  • Phase boxes: Visual grouping of flows by phase with color-coded depth
  • Interactive SVG: Hover effects on participants, messages, and flow dots
  • Animation effects: Pulse and glow for error/warning/highlight presets
  • Built-in examples: OAuth 2.0, PKCE, OIDC, MCP, A2A
  • CLI tool for validation and diagram generation
  • Go library for programmatic use
  • Conditional flows with condition field for when clauses
  • Alternative paths with alternatives for error handling and branching
  • Annotations with typed notes (security, performance, deprecated, etc.)
  • Nested phases with parent hierarchy support
  • State model with entity states and state transitions
  • State diagrams via Mermaid stateDiagram-v2 output
  • Protocol composition with imports and inheritance
  • Protocol simulation with state tracking and execution traces
  • Protocol comparison (diff) for change detection
  • Interactive debugger for step-through protocol execution
  • Security analysis with attack surface detection rules

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
{
  "protocol": {
    "id": "simple-request",
    "name": "Simple Request/Response"
  },
  "entities": [
    {"id": "client", "name": "Client", "type": "client"},
    {"id": "server", "name": "Server", "type": "server"}
  ],
  "flows": [
    {"from": "client", "to": "server", "action": "request", "mode": "request"},
    {"from": "server", "to": "client", "action": "response", "mode": "response"}
  ]
}

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: go install github.com/grokify/pidl/cmd/pidl@latest

docs.title: Generate Diagrams
docs.text:
# PlantUML
pidl generate -f plantuml protocol.json

# Mermaid
pidl generate -f mermaid protocol.json

# D2
pidl generate -f d2 protocol.json

# SVG sequence diagram
pidl generate -f svg protocol.json

# Animated SVG with flow dots
pidl generate -f svg-animated --theme=dark protocol.json

# SVG with template
pidl generate -f svg --template=high-contrast protocol.json

# Network boundary diagram
pidl generate -f svg-network protocol.json

# Mermaid state diagram
pidl generate -f mermaid-state protocol.json

# State diagram for specific entity
pidl generate -f mermaid-state --entity=client protocol.json

docs.title: Protocol Architecture
docs.text: PIDL models protocols as directed graphs where nodes are entities/components and edges are interactions/relationships.

docs.title: Entity Types
docs.text:
Entity types are classified as client-side (initiators) or server-side (responders):

Type Classification Description client Client Application or service initiating requests user Client Human actor browser Client User agent / web browser agent Client AI/LLM agent delegated_agent Client Agent receiving delegated tasks (A2A) authorization_server Server Issues tokens and handles authentication resource_server Server Hosts protected resources identity_provider Server Authenticates users and issues identity assertions service_provider Server Consumes identity assertions server Server Generic server tool_server Server Exposes tools via protocol (MCP) tool Other Individual tool capability other Other Custom entity type

docs.title: Protocol Roles
docs.text:
Entities can implement protocol-specific roles:

Protocol Description Common Roles oauth OAuth 2.0 / OIDC authorization_server, client, resource_server scim SCIM Provisioning client, service_provider spiffe SPIFFE Identity workload, spire_server, spire_agent aauth Agent Authentication person_server, access_server, client idjag ID-JAG Identity client, person_server, access_server authzen AuthZEN Authorization pep, pdp, pip, pap mcp Model Context Protocol client, server, tool a2a Agent-to-Agent client_agent, remote_agent

docs.title: Deployment Components
docs.text:
Components group entities into logical deployment units:

Component Type Description Example Products idp Identity Provider Okta, Entra ID, Auth0 agent_provider AI Agent Platform Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini person_server AAuth Person Server Identity verification service access_server AAuth Access Server Token issuance service pdp Policy Decision Point OPA, Cedar, Topaz gateway API Gateway Kong, Apigee, AWS API Gateway mcp_client MCP Client Claude Code, Cursor mcp_server MCP Server Custom tool servers resource_api Resource API Backend services spire SPIFFE Runtime SPIRE Server/Agent

docs.title: Edges
docs.text: PIDL supports two types of edges: protocol flows (sequential actions) and trust relationships (static trust).

docs.title: Protocol Flows (Sequential Actions)
docs.text:
Flows are ordered interactions between entities that define protocol choreography. They generate sequence diagrams.

Field Description from Source entity ID to Target entity ID action Action identifier mode Flow type: request, response, redirect, callback, event, tool_call, tool_result phase Optional phase grouping condition Optional conditional execution alternatives Optional alternative paths

docs.title: Protocols
docs.text: Protocol Full Name Specification oauth OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect RFC 6749, RFC 6750, OIDC Core scim System for Cross-domain Identity Management RFC 7643, RFC 7644 spiffe Secure Production Identity Framework SPIFFE/SPIRE aauth Agent Authentication AAuth Spec idjag Identity for Just-in-time Access Grant ID-JAG Spec authzen Authorization API OpenID AuthZEN mcp Model Context Protocol MCP Specification a2a Agent-to-Agent Protocol A2A Specification

docs.title: Trust Relationships
docs.text: Type Description Direction authenticates Verifies identity A authenticates B validates Validates credentials/tokens A validates B's tokens delegates Grants delegated authority A delegates to B authorizes Grants access permissions A authorizes B issues Creates credentials/tokens A issues tokens for B trusts General trust relationship A trusts B provisions Creates/manages accounts A provisions B attests Provides identity attestation A attests B's identity

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text: Credential Description Used By x509_svid X.509 SVID certificate SPIFFE/SPIRE jwt_svid JWT SVID token SPIFFE/SPIRE jwt_assertion JWT assertion for client auth OAuth 2.0 access_token OAuth access token OAuth 2.0 id_token OIDC ID token OpenID Connect aa_agent_jwt AAuth Agent JWT AAuth aa_auth_jwt AAuth Authorization JWT AAuth mtls Mutual TLS certificate mTLS api_key API key Various

docs.title: Diagram Outputs
docs.text:
PIDL generates multiple diagram types from the same protocol definition:

Diagram Type Format Source Data Description Sequence Diagram plantuml, mermaid, d2, svg, svg-animated Flows Shows ordered interactions between entities Data Flow Diagram dot, d2-flow Flows Shows data movement between entities Architecture Diagram d2-arch Entities, Flows Shows system architecture Network Diagram svg-network Entities, Trust Levels Shows network boundaries and trust zones State Diagram mermaid-state Entity States, Flows Shows entity state machines Component Diagram (planned) Components Shows logical deployment units Trust Diagram (planned) Trust Relations Shows trust relationships between entities

docs.title: Target Protocols
docs.text:
PIDL is designed for describing:

  • Authentication/Authorization: OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML
  • Agent Protocols: MCP (Model Context Protocol), A2A (Agent-to-Agent)
  • API Flows: Multi-party API choreography

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, this project adheres to Semantic Versioning, commits follow Conventional Commits, and this changelog is generated by Structured Changelog.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Embeddable viewer: @grokify/pidl-viewer shows any walkthrough from a CDN with one script tag, by inline JSON, a URL or ?src=, isolated from the page's styles
  • Walkthrough format: pidl-walkthrough/v1 is the documented, versioned form viewers read, with a JSON Schema generated from the Go types and TypeScript types generated from the schema
  • Code samples and cURL: the viewer shows each request as HTTP, a generated curl command or SDK code from tested source regions; sample sets let each implementation keep its samples beside its own code, so a protocol document names none
  • Postman collections: pidl generate -f postman writes a runnable collection with values chained between requests, checks on every response, signed requests sent through a signing proxy, and environments per target
  • A worked OAuth 2.0 example, oauth2_api_access, exercises every walkthrough feature with messages drawn from the RFCs

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Scenario groups, variants and step IDs: groups order sections, variants follow their base, and flows carry IDs addressed as . inside fragments, for deep links (a7f4e88)
  • Narration keyed by BCP 47 language with the protocol's source language as fallback, scenario briefings, narration overrides per representation, and pronunciations merged through extends and imports (0f4e1b7)
  • A curl command for every example request, with a defined wire form for example bodies; signed requests note that their signature headers are replayed (617097f)
  • Code samples on flow examples and scenarios: inline code or a region between pidl:begin and pidl:end markers in a repository file; pidl samples resolve writes a lock file and pidl samples check fails on drift (006dde7)
  • A step with no HTTP message, such as a person approving in a browser, can carry code samples alone (31c998e)
  • Built-in examples apply their sample lock when loaded, so generating from an example name includes its code (2d95f06)
  • Sample sets (pidl-samples/v1): code samples an implementation keeps apart from the protocol document, each attached to a step by its address, resolved into the set itself and joined with Protocol.WithSampleSet (7570e74)
  • pidl samples resolve and check accept a sample set; --repo-dir reads every source from one checkout and --protocol checks every step address; generate --samples can be repeated and takes a lock or a sample set (3d76c54)
  • schema/samples.schema.json generated from pidl.SampleSet and embedded as schema.SampleSetSchemaJSON (316cde9)
  • Viewer tabs for HTTP, cURL and each sample language, remembered across steps, with highlighting and a copy button (a35c1f0)
  • postman and postman-environment output formats: a folder per scenario, chained values, checks against each example, polling for deferred responses, mock mode and environments per target (26a45c8)
  • --signer proxy sends requests with HTTP message signatures through a signing proxy: Signature, Signature-Input and Content-Digest are left for the proxy, and Signature-Key names only the scheme and, for jwt, the chained token to present; unsigned requests are sent directly (7b65b99)
  • Postman chaining captures string parameters of response headers: parameters of structured fields, and auth-params of challenges such as the scope of a WWW-Authenticate Bearer challenge (181e751)
  • ResolveOptions.FS resolves the documents that extends and imports name from an fs.FS; built-in examples that extend others are resolved when loaded (a76ac1a)
  • Walkthroughs carry "format": "pidl-walkthrough/v1"; the viewer reads any v1 walkthrough and refuses another major version (ebc8393)
  • schema/walkthrough.schema.json generated from pidl.Walkthrough in a nested module, embedded as schema.WalkthroughSchemaJSON, with the example kinds as an enum (2ca8fe5)
  • Viewer TypeScript types generated from the walkthrough schema (7011a0b)
  • The viewer loads a walkthrough from inline data, a URL or ?src=, accepting https: or same-origin URLs and fetching without credentials (a5db2f3)
  • PidlViewer.mount and an embeddable build (IIFE and ES module) that renders into a shadow root, so several viewers can share a page (9514ac4)
  • Auto-mount from a script tag's data-pidl-target, data-pidl-data and data-pidl-src attributes, with errors shown in the target (a733212)
  • The @grokify/pidl-viewer npm package with type declarations, the walkthrough schema and jsDelivr and unpkg entry points (5e97077)
  • oauth2_api_access example: the authorization code grant with PKCE, client credentials, a scope challenge, an asynchronous export and a signed request, with shared fragments, decoded JWT access tokens, step IDs, narration, a briefing and pronunciations (f3f6652)

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Scenarios: one PIDL file holds a protocol's roles and an ordered list of journeys, with shared fragments drawn as labeled boxes in every sequence format
  • Consistent ordering: roles, scenarios and steps follow the file's order in every diagram, table and outline, so decks and guides built from one file agree
  • Overview outputs: roles-by-scenario matrix, token table, and an ordered outline (Markdown and JSON) for guides and slide decks
  • Token verification fields and analyzer rules that follow each token through a scenario, demonstrated on a new AAuth draft-11 example
  • D2 sequence diagrams now render as sequence diagrams: messages are edges, responses are dashed in the flow direction, and labels are quoted so punctuation cannot break compilation
  • Unit test coverage raised from 73.5% to 89.5%: the CLI is now driven through a testable run() function, every SVG format has golden-file tests, and most library packages sit between 89% and 96%

docs.title: PIDL Specification
docs.text: Protocol Interaction Description Language v1.0

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
PIDL (Protocol Interaction Description Language) is a JSON-based DSL for describing protocol choreography. It models protocols as directed interaction graphs between entities, enabling generation of sequence diagrams, data flow diagrams, and other visualizations.

PIDL is designed for protocols where the primary concern is "who talks to whom, in what order" rather than message schemas or transport details. Target protocols include OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, MCP (Model Context Protocol), and A2A (Agent-to-Agent).

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
1. Choreography-focused: Models interactions between systems, not API endpoints
  2. Transport-agnostic: No HTTP methods, URLs, or wire formats
  3. Diagram-first: Optimized for generating visual representations
  4. JSON-native: Simple parsing, strict validation, universal tooling

docs.title: Document Structure
docs.text:
A PIDL document is a JSON object. It describes either one flow (flows) or an ordered list of named scenarios (scenarios):

{
  "protocol": { ... },
  "entities": [ ... ],
  "phases": [ ... ],
  "flows": [ ... ],
  "scenarios": [ ... ]
}
Section Required Description protocol Yes Metadata about the protocol entities Yes Participants in the protocol, in display order phases No Logical grouping of flows flows One of flows or scenarios Interactions between entities, as a single flow groups No Ordered navigation sections for scenarios (see Groups) scenarios One of flows or scenarios Named, ordered sequences of flows (see Scenarios) pronunciations No Spoken forms of terms per language (see Narration) metadata No Tokens, networks, components and trust relations

docs.title: Protocol Metadata
docs.text:
The protocol object contains metadata about the protocol being described.

{
  "protocol": {
    "id": "oauth2-authorization-code",
    "name": "OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow",
    "version": "1.0",
    "description": "OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Grant as defined in RFC 6749",
    "category": "auth",
    "references": [
      {
        "name": "RFC 6749",
        "url": "https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749"
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Protocol Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier (lowercase, alphanumeric, hyphens) name string Yes Human-readable name version string No Version of this protocol description description string No Brief description category enum No One of: auth, agent, messaging, provisioning, other references array No Links to specifications language string No BCP 47 tag of the narration source language (default en-US)

docs.title: Reference Object
docs.text: Field Type Required Description name string Yes Reference name (e.g., "RFC 6749") url string Yes URL to the reference

docs.title: Entities
docs.text:
Entities represent participants in the protocol: systems, services, actors, or trust domains.

{
  "entities": [
    {
      "id": "client",
      "name": "Client Application",
      "type": "client",
      "description": "Application requesting access to protected resources"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Entity Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier (lowercase, alphanumeric, underscores) name string Yes Human-readable display name type enum Yes Entity type classification description string No Role description

docs.title: Entity Types
docs.text: Type Description Typical Use client Application or service initiating requests OAuth clients, API consumers authorization_server Issues tokens and handles authentication OAuth/OIDC providers resource_server Hosts protected resources APIs, data services user Human actor End users, resource owners browser User agent Web browsers agent AI/LLM agent MCP agents, A2A agents tool_server Exposes tools via protocol MCP tool servers tool Individual tool MCP tools delegated_agent Agent receiving delegated tasks A2A secondary agents identity_provider Authenticates users SAML IdPs service_provider Relies on identity provider SAML SPs server Generic server General purpose other Custom entity type Extension point

docs.title: Phases
docs.text:
Phases provide optional logical grouping of flows for readability and diagram organization. Phases support hierarchical nesting via the parent field.

{
  "phases": [
    {
      "id": "authorization",
      "name": "Authorization",
      "description": "User authentication and consent"
    },
    {
      "id": "mfa",
      "name": "Multi-Factor Authentication",
      "parent": "authorization",
      "description": "Optional MFA challenge"
    },
    {
      "id": "token_exchange",
      "name": "Token Exchange",
      "description": "Exchange code for tokens"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Phase Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier name string Yes Human-readable name description string No Phase description parent string No Parent phase ID for nesting

docs.title: Phase Hierarchy
docs.text:
Phases can be nested to create hierarchical groupings:

  • A phase with no parent is a root phase
  • A phase with a parent must reference a valid phase ID
  • Circular references are not allowed
  • A phase cannot be its own parent

Phases are rendered as grouping constructs in diagrams:

  • PlantUML: Colored box containers
  • Mermaid: Colored rect blocks
  • D2: Nested groups

docs.title: Flows
docs.text:
Flows are the core semantic unit: directed interactions between entities.

{
  "flows": [
    {
      "from": "client",
      "to": "auth_server",
      "action": "token_request",
      "label": "POST /token",
      "mode": "request",
      "phase": "token_exchange",
      "description": "Exchange authorization code for access token",
      "condition": "code_valid",
      "note": "Code must be exchanged within 10 minutes",
      "annotations": [
        {"type": "security", "text": "Validate code verifier (PKCE)"}
      ],
      "alternatives": [
        {
          "condition": "code_invalid",
          "flows": [
            {"from": "auth_server", "to": "client", "action": "error", "mode": "response"}
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Flow Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description id string No Step identifier, unique within its scenario and matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$ (see Step IDs) narration object No Spoken for this step, by language (see Narration) representations object No Narration overrides for http or curl from string Yes¹ Source entity ID to string Yes¹ Target entity ID action string Yes¹ Action identifier include string No ID of a fragment scenario to insert here (scenarios only; see Include Steps) label string No Display label (defaults to action) mode enum No Interaction mode (defaults to request) phase string No Phase ID this flow belongs to description string No Detailed description sequence integer No Deprecated. Display-only step number; never affects order (see Ordering) condition string No Conditional execution clause note string No Visible note displayed on diagram annotations array No Typed annotations for tooling alternatives array No Alternative flow paths verification object No Evidentiary provenance (tier/source/citation) example object No Illustrative request, response and decoded tokens (see Flow Examples)

¹ Not set on an include step, which has include instead.

docs.title: Flow Verification
docs.text:
Records the evidentiary provenance of a flow — used for incident attack-flows where every step should trace to a source (or be marked reproduced/inferred).

Field Type Required Description tier enum Yes reported | corroborated | reproduced | partially_reproduced source string No Originating source (e.g. "OpenAI technical report", "METR") citation string No URL or reference locating the source 
{
  "from": "agent", "to": "target", "action": "exfiltrate",
  "verification": {"tier": "corroborated", "source": "METR", "citation": "https://metr.org/..."}
}

The tier vocabulary matches the aisecurity-incidents deepdive.json.

docs.title: Flow Modes
docs.text: Mode Description Diagram Representation request Synchronous request Solid arrow -> response Synchronous response Dashed arrow --> redirect HTTP redirect Solid arrow with redirect annotation callback Callback/webhook Solid arrow with callback annotation interactive Human interaction Solid arrow (user involved) event Asynchronous event Dashed arrow tool_call Tool invocation (MCP) Solid arrow with tool annotation tool_result Tool result (MCP) Dashed arrow with result annotation

docs.title: Conditional Flows
docs.text:
The condition field specifies when a flow is executed. Conditions are rendered as opt blocks in sequence diagrams.

{
  "from": "client",
  "to": "server",
  "action": "refresh_token",
  "condition": "token_expired"
}

docs.title: Annotations
docs.text:
Annotations provide typed metadata for flows. They are rendered as notes in diagrams.

{
  "annotations": [
    {
      "type": "security",
      "text": "Validate PKCE code_verifier",
      "details": "Compare SHA256(code_verifier) with stored code_challenge"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Annotation Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description type enum Yes Annotation category text string Yes Annotation message details string No Additional context

docs.title: Annotation Types
docs.text: Type Description security Security considerations performance Performance implications deprecated Deprecated functionality info General information warning Warning conditions error Error conditions

docs.title: Alternative Paths
docs.text:
The alternatives field defines branching paths from a flow. They are rendered as alt/else blocks in sequence diagrams.

{
  "from": "client",
  "to": "server",
  "action": "authenticate",
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "condition": "invalid_credentials",
      "description": "Authentication failed",
      "flows": [
        {"from": "server", "to": "client", "action": "auth_error", "mode": "response"}
      ]
    },
    {
      "condition": "mfa_required",
      "description": "Multi-factor authentication needed",
      "flows": [
        {"from": "server", "to": "client", "action": "mfa_challenge", "mode": "response"},
        {"from": "client", "to": "server", "action": "mfa_response", "mode": "request"}
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Alternative Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description condition string Yes Condition that triggers this path flows array Yes Flows in this alternative path description string No Description of this alternative

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text:
A protocol often has several journeys through the same roles: AAuth has five access modes, OAuth has several grants. Instead of one file per journey, a document can hold an ordered list of named scenarios that share the same entities, phases and metadata.

{
  "protocol": {"id": "demo", "name": "Demo"},
  "entities": [
    {"id": "person", "name": "Person", "type": "user"},
    {"id": "agent", "name": "Agent", "type": "agent"},
    {"id": "ps", "name": "Person Server", "type": "authorization_server"}
  ],
  "scenarios": [
    {
      "id": "three-party",
      "name": "PS authorization",
      "flows": [
        {"from": "agent", "to": "ps", "action": "auth_token_request"},
        {"include": "consent"},
        {"from": "ps", "to": "agent", "action": "auth_token", "mode": "response"}
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "consent",
      "name": "User consent",
      "fragment": true,
      "flows": [
        {"from": "ps", "to": "person", "action": "consent_prompt"},
        {"from": "person", "to": "ps", "action": "approve", "mode": "response"}
      ]
    }
  ]
}

A document has either flows or scenarios. A document with flows behaves as a single unnamed scenario, so existing files keep working.

docs.title: Scenario Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier, matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$ name string Yes Display name description string No Description of the scenario participants array No Entity IDs to show, in entities order. Defaults to the entities the scenario uses, including those of included fragments fragment boolean No Marks a reusable sub-flow that other scenarios include group string No ID of the group the scenario is listed under. Fragments have no group variant_of string No ID of the main scenario this one is a variant of variant_label string With variant_of Label for the variant in a toggle, such as "With user approval" narration object No Spoken when the scenario opens, by language (see Narration) briefing object No Why the scenario exists, its key points, and narration for them samples array No Code for the scenario as a whole (see Samples) flows array Yes The scenario's steps, in order

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
A document MAY declare groups, an ordered array of navigation sections, each with an id, a name and an optional description. A scenario names its section with group:

{
  "groups": [
    {"id": "identity", "name": "Agent identity"},
    {"id": "access", "name": "Access modes"}
  ],
  "scenarios": [
    {"id": "agent-identity", "name": "Agent identity", "group": "identity", "flows": [ ... ]},
    {"id": "ps-authorization", "name": "PS authorization", "group": "access", "flows": [ ... ]}
  ]
}

Groups set output order: scenarios in group order, then main scenarios without a group, then fragments (see Ordering).

docs.title: Variants
docs.text: A variant is another form of the same journey, such as an autonomous flow and the same flow with user approval. It names its base with variant_of and a short variant_label. A variant shares its base's navigation entry, follows it directly in output order, and sits in the same group. A base cannot itself be a variant or a fragment.

docs.title: Step IDs
docs.text: A flow MAY have an id, unique within its scenario. IDs give samples, narration and links a stable target that survives steps being added or moved, unlike step numbers. Inside an expanded scenario, a step from an included fragment is addressed as <include>.<id>, where <include> is the include step's id or, without one, the fragment's ID. A scenario that includes the same fragment twice gives those include steps distinct IDs. Viewers accept #<scenario>/<step-id> as well as #<scenario>/<n>.

docs.title: Include Steps and Fragments
docs.text:
A step {"include": "<scenario-id>"} inserts a fragment's flows at that point. The target must be a scenario with "fragment": true, and includes must not form a cycle. An include step may also set phase, condition, label, note, description and annotations; inlined flows inherit the include's phase and condition when they have none of their own.

Diagram formats draw an include step as a labeled box spanning the fragment's participants (PlantUML ref over, a shaded Mermaid rect, a D2 group, an SVG box), or inline the fragment's flows when expanded.

Fragments are listed after main scenarios wherever scenarios are numbered or listed, so a deck or file listing shows the journeys first and the shared pieces after them.

docs.title: Working with One Scenario
docs.text: Most outputs describe one flow. Tools select a scenario and project it into a single-flow protocol: the scenario's flows, its participants (in entities order), the phases it uses, and the shared metadata. In the Go library this is Protocol.Scenario(id, ProjectOptions{Expand: ...}); on the command line it is --scenario <id>.

docs.title: Token Verification
docs.text:
Token definitions and flow security can say who checks what, so reviews and generated tables show where each guarantee is enforced:

Field On Description verified_by token definition Entity IDs that check the token claims token definition Claims checkers rely on, each with name, checked_by and description signed_by flow security Entity that signs the request, when it is not the sender issues flow security Token IDs the flow delivers verifies flow security Token IDs the receiver checks

issues and verifies let tools follow a token through a scenario: who it was delivered to, who presents it, and who signs the request that carries it.

docs.title: Narration
docs.text:
Narration is text written to be spoken, for autoplay, audio and video. On-screen prose such as description often contains identifiers (agent_jkt, aa-auth+jwt) that read badly aloud, so narration is a separate script.

Every narration value is an object keyed by BCP 47 language tag:

{
  "protocol": {"id": "aauth", "name": "AAuth", "language": "en-US"},
  "pronunciations": {"agent_jkt": {"en-US": "agent J K T"}},
  "scenarios": [{
    "id": "agent-identity",
    "name": "Agent identity",
    "narration": {"en-US": "The agent proves who it is.", "fr-FR": "L'agent prouve son identité."},
    "briefing": {
      "why": "Resources need to know which agent is calling before deciding anything else.",
      "points": ["Every request is signed", "No server issues a token"],
      "narration": {"en-US": "Why agent identity comes first."}
    },
    "flows": [{
      "id": "sign",
      "from": "agent", "to": "resource", "action": "signed_request",
      "narration": {"en-US": "The agent signs the request with its key."},
      "representations": {
        "curl": {"narration": {"en-US": "This curl command replays the signed request."}}
      }
    }]
  }]
}
  • Source language. protocol.language (default en-US) is the language a document is written in. Every narration object includes it, and it is the fallback for any language a narration lacks.
  • Representations. A step's representations override its narration when the reader views the step as http, curl, or one of the step's sample languages. The fallback order is: the representation's narration in the chosen language, then in the source language, then the step's own narration in the chosen language, then in the source language, then description.
  • Pronunciations map a term to its spoken form per language, in the shape videoascode reads, so text-to-speech tools can use them unchanged.
  • Include steps carry no narration; their fragment's steps do.

docs.title: Flow Examples
docs.text:
A flow can carry an illustrative message for walkthrough viewers. Examples explain a protocol; they are not message schemas.

{
  "from": "agent", "to": "ps", "action": "auth_token_request",
  "example": {
    "source": "draft-11 §7.2.1",
    "kind": "draft",
    "request": {
      "method": "POST",
      "url": "https://ps.example/token",
      "headers": [
        {"name": "Content-Type", "value": "application/json"},
        {"name": "Signature-Key", "value": "sig=jwt;jwt=\"eyJ...\""}
      ],
      "body": {"resource_token": "eyJ...", "presented_token": "eyJ..."}
    },
    "tokens": [
      {"token": "resource_token", "label": "request body",
       "header": {"alg": "Ed25519", "typ": "aa-resource+jwt"},
       "payload": {"iss": "https://resource.example", "agent_jkt": "kPrK..."}}
    ],
    "note": "The PS checks agent_jkt against the key that signed this request."
  }
}
Field Required Description source Yes Citation, such as a specification section kind Yes draft: taken from the source, values aligned to the scenario; derived: written from the source's normative text request One of request, response, tokens, samples method, url, ordered headers (name, value) and a JSON body response One of request, response, tokens, samples status, ordered headers and a JSON body tokens One of request, response, tokens, samples Decoded tokens: token (a token definition ID), label, header and payload note No What the reader should notice samples One of request, response, tokens, samples Code that sends or handles the message (see Samples). A step with no HTTP message, such as a person approving in a browser, can carry samples alone

Headers are a list so they keep their order. Include steps cannot carry examples.

Wire form of a body. A body is written as JSON for readability. On the wire it is the compact JSON encoding with keys in the order written; a body written as a JSON string is sent as the string's contents, for media types that are not JSON. A Content-Digest in an example covers this wire form.

cURL. Tools generate an equivalent curl command for every example request: the method, the URL, each header in order and the wire body. curl cannot create HTTP message signatures, so a signed request's command replays the example's signature headers and says so in a leading comment.

docs.title: Samples
docs.text:
A sample is code that sends or handles a step's message, such as an SDK call, shown beside the HTTP and cURL forms. Flow examples and scenarios carry samples:

"samples": [
  {"language": "go", "label": "Agent", "role": "agent",
   "source": {"repo": "example.com/sdk", "ref": "v1.2.0",
              "path": "examples/walkthrough/federated_test.go", "region": "federated.ps-to-as"}},
  {"language": "python", "code": "client.request_auth_token(resource_token)"}
]
Field Required Description language Yes Highlighter name, such as go, typescript, python or csharp. http and curl are generated, not samples label No Distinguishes samples in one language role No Entity ID whose developer writes this code code code, source or both Inline code, or a source's code once resolved source code, source or both repo, optional ref (tag or commit), path within the repository, and region

Regions. A source names the code between pidl:begin <region> and pidl:end <region> markers, written in comments in any syntax. Marker lines of other regions inside it are dropped, common indentation is removed, and blank lines at either end are trimmed. Sources should point at tested files, so samples compile and run with each release of the code they show.

Lock file. pidl samples resolve <file> reads each source from checkouts under a root directory (default $GOPATH/src, at <root>/<repo>; with ref, the file at that ref) and writes the code and its SHA-256 to <file without .json>.samples.json. Generation reads the lock, so outputs never need the source repositories or the network. pidl samples check <file> fails when a source is not in the lock, its region is missing, or its code changed since it was resolved; CI runs it to keep samples current.

docs.title: Sample Sets
docs.text:
A protocol document describes the protocol and should not depend on any implementation of it. Code samples from an SDK belong with that SDK: a sample set keeps them in a file of its own, beside the tested code they come from, and generation joins one or more sets to the document.

{
  "format": "pidl-samples/v1",
  "protocol": "aauth",
  "name": "example-sdk-go",
  "samples": [
    {"step": "agent-identity/sign", "language": "go", "label": "Agent", "role": "agent",
     "source": {"repo": "example.com/sdk", "path": "walkthrough/agent_test.go", "region": "agent-identity.sign"}},
    {"step": "interaction/approve", "language": "go", "label": "Server",
     "source": {"repo": "example.com/sdk", "path": "walkthrough/consent_test.go", "region": "interaction.approve"}}
  ]
}
Field Required Description format Yes pidl-samples/v1 protocol No The protocol ID the set is for; a set for another protocol is refused name No The implementation's name, cited by examples the set creates samples Yes Samples, each with the fields of a sample plus step, and sha256 once resolved
  • Step addresses name a step as written: <scenario>/<step-id> for a step of a scenario or a fragment, <scenario> for the scenario's own samples, or <step-id> in a document without scenarios. A sample on a fragment's step appears wherever the fragment is included. Steps need IDs to be addressed.
  • Joining. A set's samples follow a step's own samples. A step without an example gets one holding only the samples, citing the set's name. An address that names no step, or a source that is not resolved, is an error, so a set cannot fall silently behind the protocol.
  • Resolving. A set is its own lock: pidl samples resolve <set> writes each source's code and sha256 into the set, and pidl samples check <set> fails when one is missing or its source changed. --repo-dir <dir> reads every source from one checkout, such as the implementation's own repository in its CI, and --protocol <document> also checks every address.
  • Generating. pidl generate --samples <set>, repeated for several implementations, joins sets to the document for walkthrough-json and viewer.

The schema is schema/samples.schema.json.

docs.title: Ordering
docs.text:
Order in PIDL comes from one source: the position of an item in its JSON array. Every output generated from a document (diagrams, tables, outlines, file listings) uses the same order, so presentations, guides and diagrams built from one file agree.

  1. Roles follow the order of entities. Diagram columns, role tables and any other list of entities use this order.
  2. Scenarios follow the order of scenarios, arranged by groups when present: grouped scenarios in group order, then main scenarios without a group, with each variant directly after its base, then fragments. Within each section, the order of scenarios applies.
  3. Phases follow the order of phases.
  4. Messages follow the order of flows (top-level or within a scenario). An include step expands in place.
  5. Derived lists keep the order of the array they come from. A subset of entities (such as a scenario's participants or a token's checkers) is listed in entities order, never in the order written.
  6. Collections keyed by name are arrays of objects with an id. The one exception is metadata.networks, a map kept for compatibility, which tools never read in map iteration order:
  7. Network boundaries are ordered by metadata.network_layout.order first. Boundaries it does not list follow by style (external, dmz, trusted, cloud, default) and then by ID.
  8. An entity listed in more than one network belongs to the network whose ID sorts last.
  9. Entities inside each boundary follow entities order, like every other list of entities. To list them alphabetically, sort the entities array.

Numeric ordering fields are not used. The sequence field on a flow is deprecated: it is a display-only step number, and tools must not sort by it.

docs.title: Validation Rules
docs.text:
1. All entity IDs referenced in flows must be defined in entities
  2. All phase IDs referenced in flows must be defined in phases
  3. A protocol must have at least 2 entities
  4. A protocol must have at least 1 flow, or at least 1 scenario that is not a fragment; a document with scenarios has no top-level flows
  5. Entity, phase and scenario IDs must be unique within their respective arrays
  6. IDs must match pattern: ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ (entities/phases) or ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$ (protocol/scenarios)
  7. A scenario must have a name and at least 1 flow
  8. A flow is either a message (from, to, action) or an include step, and include steps appear only in scenarios
  9. An include must name a fragment scenario, and includes must not form a cycle
  10. A scenario's participants must name known entities, once each, in entities order, and must cover every entity the scenario uses
  11. Token and entity references in verified_by, claims, signed_by, issues and verifies must resolve
  12. Group IDs are unique and match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$; a scenario's group names a declared group, and fragments have no group
  13. variant_of names a main scenario that is not itself a variant, in the same group, and variant_label is set exactly when variant_of is
  14. Flow IDs match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$ and are unique within their flow list, and step IDs stay unique once fragments are expanded
  15. Narration keys are BCP 47 language tags with non-empty text, and every narration object includes the source language; representation keys are http, curl or a sample language on the step; include steps carry no narration
  16. A sample has a language other than http and curl, code or source (or both, once resolved), a known role, and a source path inside its repository

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
The canonical JSON Schema is available at:

  • Repository: schema/pidl.schema.json
  • URL: https://github.com/grokify/pidl/schema/pidl.schema.json

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Minimal OAuth 2.0 token exchange:

{
  "protocol": {
    "id": "oauth2-token-exchange",
    "name": "OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange"
  },
  "entities": [
    {"id": "client", "name": "Client", "type": "client"},
    {"id": "auth", "name": "Auth Server", "type": "authorization_server"}
  ],
  "flows": [
    {"from": "client", "to": "auth", "action": "token_request", "mode": "request"},
    {"from": "auth", "to": "client", "action": "token_response", "mode": "response"}
  ]
}

docs.title: File Extension
docs.text: PIDL files use the .pidl.json extension by convention.

docs.title: Process Profile
docs.text: PIDL supports a process profile for describing data processing workflows in addition to the standard protocol profile. Process specs model step-by-step data transformations with explicit input/output ports, processing characteristics, and failure handling.

docs.title: Protocol Kind
docs.text:
The kind field in the protocol metadata distinguishes between protocol and process specifications:

{
  "protocol": {
    "id": "etl-pipeline",
    "name": "ETL Pipeline",
    "kind": "process"
  }
}
Kind Description protocol Standard protocol (default) - models interactions between systems process Process specification - models data processing workflows

docs.title: Step Types
docs.text:
In process specifications, entities represent processing steps. The step_type field classifies each step:

{
  "entities": [
    {
      "id": "extract",
      "name": "Data Extraction",
      "type": "server",
      "step_type": "deterministic"
    },
    {
      "id": "transform",
      "name": "LLM Transform",
      "type": "server",
      "step_type": "llm"
    }
  ]
}
Step Type Icon Description Characteristics deterministic ⚙️ Predictable processing Same input → same output llm 🧠 AI/ML processing Non-deterministic, may require validation human 👤 Human involvement Manual review, approval, or input external ☁️ External services API calls, third-party services tool 🔧 Tool invocations Function calls, utilities

docs.title: Data Ports
docs.text:
Entities can define input and output data ports for explicit data flow modeling:

{
  "entities": [
    {
      "id": "transform",
      "name": "Transform Step",
      "step_type": "llm",
      "inputs": [
        {
          "name": "raw_data",
          "kind": "object",
          "required": true,
          "description": "Raw input data to transform"
        }
      ],
      "outputs": [
        {
          "name": "processed_data",
          "kind": "object",
          "description": "Transformed output data"
        },
        {
          "name": "audit_log",
          "kind": "file",
          "sensitive": true,
          "description": "Processing audit trail"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Data Port Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description name string Yes Port identifier kind enum Yes Data type classification description string No Port description required boolean No Whether input is required (default: false) sensitive boolean No Contains sensitive data (default: false) schema string No JSON Schema reference for validation

docs.title: Data Port Kinds
docs.text: Kind Icon Description file 📄 File-based data object 📦 In-memory object/struct api 🌐 API request/response database 🗄️ Database record/query queue 📬 Message queue item stream 🌊 Streaming data

docs.title: Processing Configuration
docs.text:
The processing field configures step execution characteristics:

{
  "entities": [
    {
      "id": "llm_step",
      "name": "LLM Processing",
      "step_type": "llm",
      "processing": {
        "engine": "claude-3-opus",
        "deterministic": false,
        "timeout": "PT30S",
        "cache_key": "input_hash",
        "max_retries": 3
      }
    }
  ]
}
Field Type Description engine string Processing engine identifier deterministic boolean Whether output is deterministic timeout string ISO 8601 duration (e.g., "PT30S") cache_key string Cache key expression max_retries integer Maximum retry attempts

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
The failure_modes field documents potential failure scenarios:

{
  "entities": [
    {
      "id": "external_api",
      "name": "External API Call",
      "step_type": "external",
      "failure_modes": [
        {
          "id": "timeout",
          "name": "Request Timeout",
          "severity": "medium",
          "recovery": "Retry with exponential backoff"
        },
        {
          "id": "rate_limit",
          "name": "Rate Limited",
          "severity": "low",
          "recovery": "Wait and retry"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
Field Type Required Description id string Yes Failure mode identifier name string Yes Human-readable name description string No Detailed description severity enum No critical, high, medium, low recovery string No Recovery strategy description

docs.title: Retry Strategy
docs.text:
The retry_strategy field configures automatic retry behavior:

{
  "entities": [
    {
      "id": "api_call",
      "name": "API Call",
      "step_type": "external",
      "retry_strategy": {
        "max_attempts": 3,
        "initial_delay": "PT1S",
        "max_delay": "PT30S",
        "backoff_multiplier": 2.0,
        "retryable_errors": ["timeout", "rate_limit"]
      }
    }
  ]
}
Field Type Description max_attempts integer Maximum retry attempts initial_delay string Initial delay (ISO 8601 duration) max_delay string Maximum delay between retries backoff_multiplier number Exponential backoff multiplier retryable_errors array Error types that trigger retry

docs.title: Process Spec Example
docs.text:
Complete ETL pipeline example:

{
  "protocol": {
    "id": "etl-pipeline",
    "name": "ETL Pipeline",
    "kind": "process",
    "description": "Extract, transform, and load data pipeline"
  },
  "entities": [
    {
      "id": "extract",
      "name": "Extract",
      "type": "server",
      "step_type": "deterministic",
      "outputs": [
        {"name": "raw_data", "kind": "object"}
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "transform",
      "name": "Transform",
      "type": "server",
      "step_type": "llm",
      "inputs": [
        {"name": "raw_data", "kind": "object", "required": true}
      ],
      "outputs": [
        {"name": "processed_data", "kind": "object"}
      ],
      "processing": {
        "engine": "claude-3-opus",
        "deterministic": false,
        "timeout": "PT60S"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "validate",
      "name": "Human Review",
      "type": "server",
      "step_type": "human",
      "inputs": [
        {"name": "processed_data", "kind": "object", "required": true}
      ],
      "outputs": [
        {"name": "approved_data", "kind": "object"}
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "load",
      "name": "Load",
      "type": "server",
      "step_type": "external",
      "inputs": [
        {"name": "approved_data", "kind": "object", "required": true}
      ],
      "failure_modes": [
        {"id": "connection_error", "name": "Connection Error", "severity": "high"}
      ],
      "retry_strategy": {
        "max_attempts": 3,
        "initial_delay": "PT5S",
        "backoff_multiplier": 2.0
      }
    }
  ],
  "flows": [
    {"from": "extract", "to": "transform", "action": "send_data"},
    {"from": "transform", "to": "validate", "action": "review"},
    {"from": "validate", "to": "load", "action": "approve"}
  ]
}

Rule Severity Description SEC011 Medium LLM step without downstream validation SEC012 High Sensitive data flows to LLM step SEC013 Medium Non-deterministic step in critical path SEC014 Low External step without failure modes SEC015 Medium Human step without timeout

docs.title: Design: SVG Renderer with Animation Support
docs.text: Status: Draft Author: John Wang Created: 2025-05-17 Last Updated: 2025-05-17

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Add SVG rendering capabilities to PIDL, including static sequence diagrams, animated flow visualizations with moving dots, and network boundary diagrams. This extends the existing render/ package to output self-contained SVG files with optional CSS animations.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
Current PIDL renderers output text-based diagram formats (Mermaid, PlantUML, D2, Dot) that require external tools to render. Direct SVG output provides:

  1. Self-contained output - No external rendering tools needed
  2. Animation support - CSS-based flow animations (moving dots) for visualizing data flow
  3. Network boundary views - Architecture diagrams showing trust boundaries and network segments
  4. Embeddable - Works in HTML documents, datasheets, presentations
  5. Themeable - CSS custom properties for light/dark themes
  6. Print-friendly - Static fallback for print media

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Protocol datasheets with embedded diagrams
  • Documentation with animated flow visualizations
  • Architecture diagrams showing network boundaries
  • LinkedIn/social media posts with animated protocol flows
  • Interactive documentation

docs.title: Proposed Formats
docs.text:
Extend render.Format with three new SVG variants:

Format Output Description svg Static SVG Sequence diagram similar to Mermaid output svg-animated Animated SVG Sequence diagram with CSS animations (moving dots) svg-network Network SVG Architecture diagram with boundaries and components 
const (
    FormatSVG         Format = "svg"
    FormatSVGAnimated Format = "svg-animated"
    FormatSVGNetwork  Format = "svg-network"
)

docs.text:
render/

    ├── layout.go          # participant/message layout calculations
    ├── animation.go       # CSS animation generation
    ├── theme.go           # CSS custom properties / theming
    ├── boundary.go        # network boundary inference/layout
    ├── templates.go       # template loading and registration
    └── templates/         # embedded template resources
        ├── default/
        │   ├── template.svg
        │   ├── styles.css
        │   └── config.json
        ├── sketch/
        │   ├── template.svg
        │   ├── styles.css
        │   └── config.json
        ├── minimal/
        │   └── ...
        ├── blueprint/
        │   └── ...
        └── high-contrast/
            └── ...

docs.title: Renderer Interface
docs.text:
The new renderers implement the existing Renderer interface:

type SVGRenderer struct {
    // Animated enables CSS animations (moving dots along message lines)
    Animated bool

    // Theme selects color scheme ("light", "dark", "auto")
    Theme string

    // Width sets the SVG width (default: auto-calculated)
    Width int

    // ParticipantSpacing sets horizontal spacing between participants
    ParticipantSpacing int

    // MessageSpacing sets vertical spacing between messages
    MessageSpacing int

    // ShowPhases renders phase boxes as background regions
    ShowPhases bool

    // AnimationDuration sets the flow animation duration (default: 2s)
    AnimationDuration time.Duration

    // AnimationStagger staggers animation start times per message
    AnimationStagger bool
}

type SVGNetworkRenderer struct {
    // Animated enables CSS animations
    Animated bool

    // Theme selects color scheme
    Theme string

    // Boundaries defines network boundary regions
    // If empty, auto-detected from entity metadata
    Boundaries []NetworkBoundary

    // Layout algorithm ("horizontal", "vertical", "auto")
    Layout string
}

type NetworkBoundary struct {
    ID       string
    Name     string
    Entities []string  // entity IDs within this boundary
    Style    string    // "trusted", "dmz", "external"
}

docs.title: SVG Elements
docs.text:
<svg viewBox="0 0 800 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <style>
    /* CSS custom properties for theming */
    :root { --color-primary: #1a365d; ... }

    /* Animation keyframes */
    @keyframes flow {
      0% { offset-distance: 0%; }
      100% { offset-distance: 100%; }
    }
    .flow-dot { animation: flow 2s linear infinite; }
  </style>

  <defs>
    <!-- Reusable elements: arrows, gradients -->
    <marker id="arrow" ...>
  </defs>

  <!-- Participants -->
  <g class="participants">
    <rect class="participant-box" x="50" y="10" width="100" height="30"/>
    <text class="participant-text">Human</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Lifelines -->
  <g class="lifelines">
    <line class="lifeline" x1="100" y1="40" x2="100" y2="380"/>
  </g>

  <!-- Messages with optional animation -->
  <g class="messages">
    <path id="msg1" class="message-line" d="M100,60 L250,60"/>
    <text class="message-text">1. Authenticate</text>

    <!-- Animated dot (only in svg-animated) -->
    <circle class="flow-dot" r="4" style="offset-path: path('M100,60 L250,60')"/>
  </g>
</svg>

docs.title: CSS Offset Path Animation
docs.text:
Use CSS offset-path to animate dots along message paths:

@keyframes flow {
  0% { offset-distance: 0%; }
  100% { offset-distance: 100%; }
}

.flow-dot {
  offset-rotate: 0deg;
  animation: flow var(--animation-duration, 2s) linear infinite;
}

/* Staggered animation delays */
.flow-dot[data-step="1"] { animation-delay: 0s; }
.flow-dot[data-step="2"] { animation-delay: 0.5s; }
.flow-dot[data-step="3"] { animation-delay: 1s; }

docs.title: Animation Options
docs.text: Option Description Default --animation-duration Total animation cycle time 2s --dot-size Radius of animated dots 4px --dot-color Dot fill color var(--color-accent) stagger Delay between message animations 0.5s direction forward, reverse, alternate forward

docs.title: Print Media
docs.text:
Animations are disabled in print:

@media print {
  .flow-dot { display: none; }
  /* Or show as static dots at midpoint */
  .flow-dot {
    animation: none;
    offset-distance: 50%;
  }
}

docs.title: Network Boundaries
docs.text: Network boundaries group entities into logical regions (trust zones, network segments, deployment environments). The renderer supports both automatic inference and explicit configuration.

docs.title: Inference + Override Model
docs.text:
Boundaries follow a layered approach:

  1. Inference (default): If entities have metadata.network, group them automatically
  2. Override: Explicit metadata.networks section takes precedence
  3. CLI override: --boundary flags override everything

This allows sensible defaults while giving humans/LLMs full control when needed.

docs.title: Template Configuration
docs.text:
config.json defines layout and rendering parameters:

{
  "name": "sketch",
  "description": "Hand-drawn informal style",
  "layout": {
    "participant_spacing": 150,
    "message_spacing": 50,
    "padding": 20,
    "participant_box": {
      "width": 120,
      "height": 40,
      "corner_radius": 8
    }
  },
  "fonts": {
    "primary": "Architects Daughter, cursive",
    "mono": "Comic Mono, monospace"
  },
  "line_style": {
    "stroke_width": 2,
    "hand_drawn": true,
    "wobble_factor": 0.3
  },
  "animation": {
    "dot_shape": "circle",
    "dot_size": 6,
    "trail_enabled": true
  }
}

docs.title: Using Templates
docs.text:
CLI: 

pidl render --format=svg --template=sketch protocol.json
pidl render --format=svg-animated --template=minimal protocol.json

Go API: 

renderer := render.NewSVG()
renderer.Template = "sketch"
renderer.RenderString(protocol)

docs.title: Custom Templates
docs.text:
Users can provide custom templates:

# From directory
pidl render --format=svg --template-dir=./my-template protocol.json

# Register in config
pidl config set templates.corporate=/path/to/corporate-template
pidl render --format=svg --template=corporate protocol.json

docs.title: Template Variables
docs.text:
Templates can use variables for customization:

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <style>
    :root {
      --brand-primary: {{.BrandPrimary | default "#1a365d"}};
      --brand-secondary: {{.BrandSecondary | default "#2c5282"}};
      --font-family: {{.FontFamily | default "Inter, sans-serif"}};
    }
  </style>
  <!-- ... -->
</svg>

pidl render --format=svg --template=corporate \
  --set brand-primary="#ff6600" \
  --set brand-secondary="#333333" \
  protocol.json

docs.title: Per-Message Animation Control
docs.text: Animation can be configured globally and overridden per-flow (message). This enables highlighting critical paths, color-coding by outcome, or keeping setup flows static.

docs.title: Flow Animation Schema
docs.text:
Extend the PIDL flow schema with optional animation field:

{
  "flows": [
    {
      "from": "agent",
      "to": "idp",
      "label": "1. Request ID-JAG",
      "animation": {
        "enabled": true,
        "duration": "1.5s",
        "dot_color": "#3182ce",
        "dot_size": 5
      }
    },
    {
      "from": "idp",
      "to": "agent",
      "label": "2. Return ID-JAG",
      "mode": "response",
      "animation": {
        "enabled": true,
        "dot_color": "#68d391",
        "delay": "0.5s"
      }
    },
    {
      "from": "agent",
      "to": "resource",
      "label": "3. Access API",
      "animation": {
        "enabled": true,
        "dot_color": "#3182ce"
      }
    },
    {
      "from": "resource",
      "to": "agent",
      "label": "4. 403 Forbidden",
      "mode": "response",
      "animation": {
        "enabled": true,
        "dot_color": "#fc8181",
        "pulse": true
      }
    },
    {
      "from": "human",
      "to": "agent",
      "label": "Setup: Delegate task",
      "animation": {
        "enabled": false
      }
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "animation": {
      "default_enabled": true,
      "default_duration": "2s",
      "default_dot_color": "#3182ce",
      "stagger": "0.3s",
      "loop": true
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Animation Properties
docs.text: Property Type Default Description enabled boolean true Enable/disable animation for this flow duration string "2s" Animation cycle duration delay string "0s" Start delay (for sequencing) dot_color string theme accent Dot fill color dot_size number 4 Dot radius in pixels dot_shape string "circle" Shape: circle, square, diamond, arrow pulse boolean false Add pulsing effect (for errors/warnings) trail boolean false Show fading trail behind dot direction string "forward" forward, reverse, alternate easing string "linear" CSS easing: linear, ease-in-out, etc.

docs.title: Semantic Presets
docs.text:
For convenience, use semantic presets:

{
  "flows": [
    {
      "from": "agent", "to": "resource",
      "label": "API Call",
      "animation": "request"
    },
    {
      "from": "resource", "to": "agent",
      "label": "Success",
      "animation": "success"
    },
    {
      "from": "resource", "to": "agent",
      "label": "Error",
      "animation": "error"
    },
    {
      "from": "human", "to": "agent",
      "label": "Background",
      "animation": "none"
    }
  ]
}

Preset definitions:

Preset Color Effect Use Case request Blue Standard Outgoing requests response Gray Dashed path Return values success Green Standard Successful operations error Red Pulse Errors, failures warning Orange Pulse Warnings highlight Yellow Glow + larger dot Critical path background Gray, 50% opacity Subtle Setup/teardown none N/A Static arrow No animation

docs.title: Global Animation Settings
docs.text:
Set defaults in protocol metadata:

{
  "metadata": {
    "animation": {
      "default_enabled": true,
      "default_duration": "2s",
      "stagger": "0.3s",
      "stagger_mode": "sequential",
      "loop": true,
      "pause_on_hover": true,
      "color_scheme": {
        "request": "#3182ce",
        "response": "#a0aec0",
        "success": "#68d391",
        "error": "#fc8181",
        "warning": "#f6ad55"
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Stagger Modes
docs.text: Mode Description sequential Each flow starts after previous ends overlap Flows start with fixed delay, may overlap parallel All flows animate simultaneously phase Flows within same phase animate together

docs.title: Generated CSS Example
docs.text:
For a flow with custom animation:

/* Flow: agent → idp (step 1) */
#flow-1-dot {
  fill: #3182ce;
  r: 5;
  offset-path: path('M150,80 L300,80');
  offset-rotate: 0deg;
  animation: flow-1 1.5s linear infinite;
  animation-delay: 0s;
}

@keyframes flow-1 {
  0% { offset-distance: 0%; }
  100% { offset-distance: 100%; }
}

/* Flow: resource → agent (step 4, error) */
#flow-4-dot {
  fill: #fc8181;
  r: 4;
  offset-path: path('M550,140 L150,140');
  animation: flow-4 2s linear infinite, pulse 0.5s ease-in-out infinite;
  animation-delay: 0.9s;
}

@keyframes pulse {
  0%, 100% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); }
  50% { opacity: 0.7; transform: scale(1.3); }
}

docs.title: CLI Integration
docs.text:
# Static SVG sequence diagram
pidl render --format=svg protocol.json -o diagram.svg

# Animated SVG with flow dots
pidl render --format=svg-animated protocol.json -o animated.svg

# Network boundary diagram
pidl render --format=svg-network protocol.json -o network.svg

# With template
pidl render --format=svg --template=sketch protocol.json
pidl render --format=svg-animated --template=minimal protocol.json

# Custom template from directory
pidl render --format=svg --template-dir=./my-template protocol.json

# Template with brand customization
pidl render --format=svg --template=corporate \
  --set brand-primary="#ff6600" \
  --set font-family="Helvetica" \
  protocol.json

# Animation options
pidl render --format=svg-animated \
  --theme=dark \
  --animation-duration=3s \
  --stagger=0.5s \
  --stagger-mode=sequential \
  protocol.json

# Network boundary overrides
pidl render --format=svg-network \
  --boundary="dmz:auth_server,idp" \
  --boundary="internal:resource,database" \
  --layout=horizontal \
  protocol.json

# Combined options
pidl render --format=svg-animated \
  --template=minimal \
  --theme=auto \
  --animation-duration=2s \
  --stagger \
  protocol.json -o flow.svg

docs.title: Phase 1: Static SVG Renderer ✅
docs.text:
• [x] Basic SVGRenderer struct implementing Renderer interface
  • [x] Participant layout calculation
  • [x] Lifeline rendering
  • [x] Message arrows (solid for requests, dashed for responses)
  • [x] Message labels with step numbers
  • [x] Light/dark theme support via CSS custom properties
  • [ ] Default template (default/)
  • [x] Unit tests and golden file tests

docs.title: Phase 2: CSS Animation Support ✅
docs.text:
• [x] offset-path animation for flow dots
  • [x] Global animation configuration (metadata.animation)
  • [x] Per-message animation properties (flow.animation)
  • [x] Semantic presets (request, success, error, none)
  • [x] Stagger modes (sequential, overlap, parallel)
  • [x] Print media fallback (static or hidden dots)
  • [ ] Browser compatibility testing (Chrome, Firefox, Safari)

docs.title: Phase 3: Template System ✅
docs.text:
• [x] Template loading from embedded FS
  • [x] Template configuration parsing (config.json)
  • [x] Built-in templates: default, minimal, sketch, blueprint, dark
  • [x] Custom template loading from directory
  • [ ] Template variable substitution
  • [x] CLI --template and --template-dir flags
  • [ ] Template validation

docs.title: Phase 4: Network Boundary Diagrams ✅
docs.text:
• [x] SVGNetworkRenderer implementation
  • [x] Boundary inference from entity.metadata.network
  • [x] Explicit boundary configuration (metadata.networks)
  • [x] Boundary region layout algorithm
  • [x] Entity placement within boundaries
  • [x] Connection routing between/across boundaries
  • [x] Boundary styles (trusted, dmz, external, cloud)

docs.title: Phase 5: Advanced Features
docs.text:
• [ ] Phase boxes/regions in sequence diagrams
  • [ ] Alternative paths visualization
  • [ ] High-contrast template for accessibility
  • [ ] Interactive hover states (optional, CSS-only)
  • [ ] Animation pulse/glow effects for errors
  • [ ] Export to GIF/WebP documentation (via Puppeteer/ffmpeg)

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
1. Unit tests - Layout calculations, SVG element generation
  2. Golden file tests - Compare generated SVG against expected output
  3. Visual regression - Screenshot comparison (optional, CI integration)
  4. Browser testing - Verify animations in Chrome, Firefox, Safari

docs.title: 1. SMIL Animations (rejected)
docs.text:
• Deprecated in Chrome, inconsistent browser support
  • CSS animations have better support and performance

docs.title: 2. JavaScript Animations (rejected)
docs.text:
• Requires runtime, not self-contained
  • CSS offset-path provides sufficient capability

docs.title: 3. External Tools (partial)
docs.text:
• Keep as option: export SVG, use external tool for GIF conversion
  • Puppeteer/Playwright can capture animated SVG as video/GIF

docs.title: Resolved Questions
docs.text:
1. Should svg-network infer boundaries from entity metadata, or require explicit configuration?

Resolution: Both. Use inference by default from entity.metadata.network, but allow explicit override via metadata.networks[id].entities or CLI --boundary flags. See Network Boundaries section.

  1. Should we support custom SVG templates for different visual styles?

Resolution: Yes. Support built-in templates (default, sketch, minimal, etc.) and custom templates from directories. Templates include SVG structure, CSS styling, and layout config. See Custom SVG Templates section.

  1. Should animation be configurable per-message (e.g., some flows animate, others don't)?

Resolution: Yes. Each flow can have an animation field with properties like enabled, dot_color, duration, pulse. Also support semantic presets (request, success, error, none). See Per-Message Animation Control section.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
1. Should templates support JavaScript for advanced interactivity, or keep SVG/CSS only for maximum portability?
  2. Should we provide a template authoring guide or template validation tool?
  3. Should animation presets be customizable in user config, or only in protocol metadata?
  4. Should we support exporting animation frames for GIF generation, or rely on external tools?

docs.title: A2A Agent Delegation
docs.text:
Agent-to-Agent delegation protocol.

pidl generate a2a_agent_delegation

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A2A (Agent-to-Agent) enables agents to delegate tasks to other agents, with optional human authorization.

docs.title: Entities
docs.text: Entity Type Role user user Human authorizing delegation primary_agent agent Agent requesting delegation delegated_agent delegated_agent Agent receiving delegated task

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. Delegation Request: Primary agent requests task delegation
  2. Human Authorization: User authorizes the delegation (optional)
  3. Task Execution: Delegated agent executes task
  4. Result Return: Result returned to primary agent

docs.title: agent
docs.text: The primary AI agent initiating interactions.

docs.title: delegated_agent
docs.text: An agent that receives delegated tasks from other agents. Has limited scope based on delegation permissions.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "protocol": {
    "id": "a2a-agent-delegation",
    "name": "A2A Agent Delegation",
    "category": "agent"
  },
  "entities": [
    {"id": "user", "name": "User", "type": "user"},
    {"id": "primary", "name": "Primary Agent", "type": "agent"},
    {"id": "delegated", "name": "Delegated Agent", "type": "delegated_agent"}
  ],
  "phases": [
    {"id": "auth", "name": "Authorization"},
    {"id": "exec", "name": "Execution"}
  ],
  "flows": [
    {
      "from": "primary",
      "to": "user",
      "action": "request_delegation",
      "phase": "auth"
    },
    {
      "from": "user",
      "to": "primary",
      "action": "authorize",
      "mode": "interactive",
      "phase": "auth"
    },
    {
      "from": "primary",
      "to": "delegated",
      "action": "delegate_task",
      "phase": "exec"
    },
    {
      "from": "delegated",
      "to": "primary",
      "action": "task_result",
      "mode": "response",
      "phase": "exec"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: With Alternatives
docs.text:
Handling delegation rejection:

{
  "from": "primary",
  "to": "user",
  "action": "request_delegation",
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "condition": "rejected",
      "flows": [
        {"from": "user", "to": "primary", "action": "rejection", "mode": "response"}
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Infographic Examples
docs.text: PIDL can generate compact, visually appealing infographics optimized for social media (LinkedIn) and datasheets.

docs.title: OAuth 2.0 PKCE (LinkedIn Square)
docs.text:
pidl generate -f infographic --ig-size=linkedin-square --ig-title="OAuth 2.0 PKCE" oauth2_pkce

Features:

  • Entity type shapes: circle for user, diamond for auth server, cylinder for resource server
  • Entity type colors matching the entity roles
  • Animated dots showing the flow of data

docs.text:
pidl generate -f infographic --ig-size=datasheet-tile --ig-theme=minimal --ig-title="ETL" etl_pipeline.json

  • Compact 400x400 size for datasheet grids
  • Minimal theme with subtle colors
  • Step type icons (gear for deterministic, cloud for external)

pidl generate -f infographic --ig-size=linkedin-square --ig-theme=tech --ig-title="CI/CD Pipeline" ci_cd_pipeline.json

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
1. LinkedIn posts: Use linkedin-square (1200x1200) for maximum visibility in feeds
  2. Link previews: Use linkedin-landscape (1200x627) for shared links

docs.title: MCP Tool Invocation
docs.text:
Model Context Protocol tool invocation flow.

pidl generate mcp_tool_invocation

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: MCP (Model Context Protocol) enables AI agents to invoke tools provided by tool servers.

docs.title: Entities
docs.text: Entity Type Role agent agent AI/LLM agent tool_server tool_server Exposes tools via MCP

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. Tool Discovery: Agent discovers available tools
  2. Tool Invocation: Agent calls a tool
  3. Tool Result: Server returns result

docs.title: Flow Modes
docs.text: Mode Use tool_call Agent invoking a tool tool_result Server returning result

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "protocol": {
    "id": "mcp-tool-invocation",
    "name": "MCP Tool Invocation",
    "category": "agent"
  },
  "entities": [
    {"id": "agent", "name": "AI Agent", "type": "agent"},
    {"id": "tool_server", "name": "Tool Server", "type": "tool_server"}
  ],
  "flows": [
    {
      "from": "agent",
      "to": "tool_server",
      "action": "list_tools",
      "mode": "request"
    },
    {
      "from": "tool_server",
      "to": "agent",
      "action": "tools_list",
      "mode": "response"
    },
    {
      "from": "agent",
      "to": "tool_server",
      "action": "invoke_tool",
      "mode": "tool_call"
    },
    {
      "from": "tool_server",
      "to": "agent",
      "action": "tool_result",
      "mode": "tool_result"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Authorization Code Flow
docs.text:
The standard OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Grant.

pidl generate oauth2_authorization_code

docs.title: Entities
docs.text: Entity Type Role user user Resource owner browser browser User agent client client Application requesting access auth_server authorization_server Issues tokens resource_server resource_server Protected API

docs.title: Phases
docs.text:
1. Authorization Request: User initiates login
  2. User Authentication: User authenticates with auth server
  3. Authorization Grant: User consents to access
  4. Token Exchange: Client exchanges code for tokens
  5. Resource Access: Client accesses protected resources

docs.title: PKCE Flow
docs.text:
OAuth 2.0 with Proof Key for Code Exchange for public clients.

docs.title: Additional Security
docs.text:
• code_verifier: Random string generated by client
  • code_challenge: SHA256 hash of verifier
  • Server validates verifier matches challenge

      "text": "Validate code_verifier against code_challenge"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Use as Go Library
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/grokify/pidl"
    "github.com/grokify/pidl/render"
)

func main() {
    // Parse a PIDL file
    p, err := pidl.ParseFile("protocol.json")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    // Validate
    if errs := p.Validate(); errs.HasErrors() {
        log.Fatal(errs)
    }

    // Generate Mermaid diagram
    diagram, err := render.RenderString(render.FormatMermaid, p)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    fmt.Println(diagram)
}

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Alternatives define branching paths from a flow point, rendered as alt/else blocks in sequence diagrams.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
{
  "from": "client",
  "to": "server",
  "action": "authenticate",
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "condition": "invalid_credentials",
      "description": "Authentication failed",
      "flows": [
        {"from": "server", "to": "client", "action": "auth_error", "mode": "response"}
      ]
    },
    {
      "condition": "mfa_required",
      "description": "Multi-factor authentication needed",
      "flows": [
        {"from": "server", "to": "client", "action": "mfa_challenge", "mode": "response"},
        {"from": "client", "to": "server", "action": "mfa_response", "mode": "request"}
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Alternative Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description condition string Yes Condition that triggers this path flows array Yes Flows in this alternative path (min 1) description string No Description of this alternative

docs.title: Mermaid
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    client->>server: authenticate
    alt invalid_credentials
        server-->>client: auth_error
    else mfa_required
        server-->>client: mfa_challenge
        client->>server: mfa_response
    end

docs.title: PlantUML
docs.text:
client -> server: authenticate
alt invalid_credentials
    server --> client: auth_error
else mfa_required
    server --> client: mfa_challenge
    client -> server: mfa_response
end

docs.title: Error Handling Pattern
docs.text:
Common pattern for request/response with error handling:

{
  "flows": [
    {
      "from": "client",
      "to": "server",
      "action": "request",
      "alternatives": [
        {
          "condition": "error",
          "flows": [
            {"from": "server", "to": "client", "action": "error_response", "mode": "response"}
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {"from": "server", "to": "client", "action": "success_response", "mode": "response"}
  ]
}

docs.title: Nested Flows
docs.text:
Alternative flows can include all flow features:

{
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "condition": "retry_needed",
      "flows": [
        {
          "from": "client",
          "to": "server",
          "action": "retry",
          "note": "Exponential backoff",
          "annotations": [
            {"type": "performance", "text": "Max 3 retries"}
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Alternative flows are validated:

  • Condition is required
  • At least one flow is required
  • Entity references must be valid
  • Phase references must be valid (if specified)

docs.title: Helper Methods (Go)
docs.text:
// Check if flow has alternatives
if flow.HasAlternatives() {
    for _, alt := range flow.Alternatives {
        fmt.Printf("Alternative: %s (%d flows)\n", alt.Condition, len(alt.Flows))
    }
}

docs.title: vs Condition
docs.text:
Feature condition alternatives Purpose Single conditional flow Multiple branching paths Rendering opt block alt/else blocks Flows Current flow only Nested flow arrays

Use condition for "execute this flow if X". Use alternatives for "branch to different paths based on conditions".

docs.title: Annotations
docs.text: Annotations provide typed metadata for flows. They are rendered as notes in diagrams.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
{
  "from": "client",
  "to": "server",
  "action": "authenticate",
  "annotations": [
    {
      "type": "security",
      "text": "Validate PKCE code_verifier",
      "details": "Compare SHA256(code_verifier) with stored code_challenge"
    },
    {
      "type": "performance",
      "text": "Cache token for TTL"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Annotation Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description type enum Yes Annotation category text string Yes Annotation message details string No Additional context

docs.title: Annotation Types
docs.text: Type Description Use Cases security Security considerations Auth checks, encryption, validation performance Performance implications Caching, timeouts, rate limits deprecated Deprecated functionality Legacy endpoints, migration notes info General information Documentation, explanations warning Warning conditions Edge cases, prerequisites error Error conditions Failure modes, error handling

docs.title: Diagram Rendering
docs.text: Annotations are rendered as notes in sequence diagrams:

docs.title: Mermaid
docs.text: note right of server: [SECURITY] Validate PKCE code_verifier

docs.title: PlantUML
