docs.title: TRD — Postman collections from PIDL
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-PIDL-006 Repository: github.com/grokify/pidl

docs.title: Renderer
docs.text: render/postman.go builds Postman Collection v2.1 types (info, item folders and requests, event scripts, variables, examples) from the walkthrough model, so ordering, fragment expansion and examples follow the same rules as the viewer. encoding/json writes them with stable key order.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
• One base URL variable per role (<role>_url), derived from the scheme and host of the role's example URLs.
  • One variable per chained value. A value is chained when a later request's example contains a string that an earlier response's example carries (a token, a Location, a code). The response's test script reads it from the same place (a JSON pointer into the body, or a header) and later requests use {{name}}. Names come from token definition IDs, or from the JSON member or header name.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text: Test scripts are generated, not templated by hand: pm.response.to.have.status, header presence, body member presence via JSON pointers, and token checks that split the JWT, base64url-decode the payload and assert claim names. Polling uses pm.execution.setNextRequest with a counter variable and a retry limit.

docs.title: Signer profiles
docs.text: A signer profile names how a helper receives the target and presented token. The first profile, aauth-sandbox, prefixes the URL with the helper's address and sets X-Sandbox-Present and X-Sandbox-Token from the example's Signature-Key token.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Golden collections for the AAuth example (signer and mock modes); schema validation against the v2.1 schema; a Newman run against the sandbox in the aauth-postman repository's CI.

docs.title: PLAN — Walkthrough format and embeddable viewer
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-PIDL-007 Repository: github.com/grokify/pidl

docs.title: Entry Gate
docs.text: The viewer's representations and code samples (feat/viewer-representations) delivered.

docs.title: Build Order
docs.text:
1. Format: the identifier, the generated schema and the generated TypeScript types, then the format reference page.
  2. Embeddable viewer: the loader with sources, version check and URL safety; mount and the library build; auto-mount; then the package and the embedding guide.

The format comes first so the CDN script, the first reader outside this repository, starts on a versioned contract.

docs.title: Risks and Mitigations
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Viewer CSS clashes with a host page Scope every rule under .pidl-viewer ?src= used to show misleading content under a trusted docs domain https: or same-origin only; no HTML rendering; the page shows the source URL Schema and Go types drift Generated schema with a drift test; generated TypeScript types with a CI diff A dependency in the root module Generator in a nested module

docs.title: Follow-On
docs.text: A hosted app (INIT-PIDL-008): upload or link a walkthrough or PIDL file, render it server-side, share a link. It reuses the format and the embeddable viewer.

docs.title: PRD — Walkthrough format and embeddable viewer
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-PIDL-007 Repository: github.com/grokify/pidl

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
PIDL has two formats today, but only one is documented. People write PIDL; pidl generate -f walkthrough-json turns it into a walkthrough, with extends resolved, fragments expanded, cURL commands rendered, code samples resolved and findings attached. The viewer reads only the walkthrough. Yet the walkthrough has no version, no schema, and its TypeScript types are maintained by hand, so the Go and TypeScript sides can drift, and nobody outside this repository can rely on it.

The viewer itself ships only one way: pidl generate -f viewer writes a self-contained HTML file with the walkthrough embedded. That suits offline use, but a docs site that wants to show a walkthrough has to publish a separate 250 KB page per protocol, regenerate it whenever the viewer changes, and link out instead of embedding.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• An official walkthrough format (pidl-walkthrough/v1): versioned, described by a JSON Schema generated from the Go types, with TypeScript types generated from that schema, and a written compatibility rule. Any tool can produce or read it.
  • An embeddable viewer published to npm and served by CDNs: one script tag shows a walkthrough on any page, loaded from inline JSON, a URL attribute or a ?src= query parameter.
  • One viewer, three deliveries: the self-contained HTML file (offline, local files), the CDN script (docs sites), and later a hosted app. All read the same format.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Reading PIDL source in the browser. Resolution, rendering and sample tooling stay in Go; the browser reads walkthroughs only.
  • The hosted (cloud) app. It is a later initiative that builds on the format and the embeddable viewer.
  • Publishing to npm from CI. The first releases are published by a maintainer.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. Format identifier. Every walkthrough carries "format": "pidl-walkthrough/v1" as its first field. The viewer refuses a different major version with a message naming the version it found; a walkthrough with no format (written before v1) is read as v1.
  2. Generated schema. schema/walkthrough.schema.json is generated from pidl.Walkthrough and embedded as schema.WalkthroughSchemaJSON. Property names are snake_case, matching PIDL. A check fails when the committed schema differs from the generated one.
  3. Generated TypeScript types. viewer/src/walkthrough.gen.ts is generated from the schema; the viewer imports its types from there. CI fails when it is out of date.
  4. File naming. Walkthroughs use the .walkthrough.json extension; the guides and examples use it.
  5. Compatibility rule. Within v1, changes only add optional fields; readers ignore fields they do not know. Removing or renaming a field, changing its type or meaning, or making a field required is v2.
  6. Embeddable build. npm run build:lib writes dist/pidl-viewer.js (IIFE, global PidlViewer) and dist/pidl-viewer.mjs (ES module), each with its CSS included and scoped to the viewer's root element.
  7. Mounting. PidlViewer.mount(element, { data | src }) renders a walkthrough into an element and returns a handle with unmount(). Several viewers can share a page.
  8. Auto-mount. A script tag with data-pidl-target mounts on load, reading in this order: an inline <script type="application/json"> named by data-pidl-data, the URL in data-pidl-src, then the page's ?src= parameter.
  9. Relative URLs. Paths inside a walkthrough loaded from a URL resolve against that URL, not the page.
  10. Untrusted input. A walkthrough is data. The viewer renders no HTML from it, opens only http: and https: links, and ?src= loads only https: URLs, or same-origin ones.
  11. Package. @grokify/pidl-viewer on npm with the two builds, the generated types and the schema, versioned with pidl.
  12. Guide. A page on embedding the viewer, with CDN snippets for inline data, a URL and ?src=, and the CORS requirement.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• pidl generate -f walkthrough-json output validates against the embedded schema for every built-in example.
  • A plain HTML page with one script tag from jsDelivr shows the AAuth walkthrough from a GitHub Pages URL.
  • The self-contained viewer HTML and the CDN script render the same walkthrough identically.

docs.title: TRD — Walkthrough format and embeddable viewer
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-PIDL-007 Repository: github.com/grokify/pidl

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
{
  "format": "pidl-walkthrough/v1",
  "id": "aauth-protocol",
  "name": "AAuth",
  "roles": [ ... ],
  "scenarios": [ ... ]
}

pidl.WalkthroughFormat holds the identifier, and Protocol.Walkthrough sets it, so every producer writes it. Readers compare the major version only: the text after /v, up to the first ..

docs.title: Schema Generation
docs.text:
The root module has no dependencies and keeps none. The generator lives in a nested module, schema/gen (go.mod with replace github.com/grokify/pidl => ../.., which stays inside the repository), using github.com/invopop/jsonschema:

  • go run ./schema/gen (run from schema/gen) reflects pidl.Walkthrough, sets $id to https://github.com/grokify/pidl/schema/walkthrough.schema.json and the title, and writes schema/walkthrough.schema.json.
  • format is a const of the identifier, so the schema documents the version it describes.
  • Fields without omitempty are required, matching what producers always write.
  • A test in schema/gen regenerates the schema in memory and fails when it differs from the committed file; CI runs it.
  • schemakit lint --property-case snake_case passes on the generated schema.

The root module embeds the file as schema.WalkthroughSchemaJSON. A root test checks that every built-in example's walkthrough has exactly the top-level fields the schema lists and that format matches the schema's const, without a validator dependency.

docs.title: TypeScript Types
docs.text: json-schema-to-typescript (dev dependency) turns the schema into viewer/src/walkthrough.gen.ts (npm run types). viewer/src/types.ts re-exports the generated types under the names the viewer uses today, so components do not change. The viewer CI job regenerates the file and fails on a diff.

docs.title: Embeddable Build
docs.text:
A second Vite configuration, vite.lib.config.ts, builds src/lib.tsx in library mode:

  • formats iife (name PidlViewer) and es; React bundled, so the page needs nothing else;
  • CSS injected by the bundle into a <style> element once per page;
  • every selector scoped under .pidl-viewer, the class the root element gets on mount.
export interface MountOptions {
  data?: Walkthrough | string;   // parsed or JSON text
  src?: string;                  // URL of a .walkthrough.json
  base?: string;                 // base for relative paths (default: src)
}
export function mount(el: Element, opts: MountOptions): Promise<{ unmount(): void }>;

Auto-mount runs when the bundle's own <script> (document.currentScript) has data-pidl-target.

docs.title: Loading and Safety
docs.text: loadWalkthrough takes a source (inline element, URL) and returns the parsed walkthrough plus its base URL. It checks format, then the required fields. ?src= accepts https: URLs, or same-origin URLs on any scheme so local development works. Fetches use credentials: "omit". The viewer uses React text rendering only; any link taken from data passes safeHref, which allows http: and https: after resolving against the base.

docs.title: Hash Navigation
docs.text: The viewer keeps navigation state in the page's hash today. When embedded, it uses the hash only when it is the sole viewer on the page and was auto-mounted; otherwise it keeps state in memory, so it does not fight the host page's routing.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Go: format constant, schema drift, examples against the schema's top-level fields.
  • Viewer: loading from inline data, URL and ?src=; version refusal; safeHref; relative base resolution; mount and unmount; two mounts on one page.
